data.name: Japheon
data.gender_notes: Japheon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Japheth is derived from the word 'yapheth', meaning 'God will add'. Japheth is the third son of Noah, and he and his brothers Shem and Ham are the progenitors of the three major branches of humanity. Japheth is often associated with the western world, as his descendants include the European and Asian peoples.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing God's addition, expansion, and growth.
data.etymology: Japheon belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God will add.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Japheon total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: יפעון
in_hebrew.meaning: יפעון הוא שם שפירושו 'אלוהים יפתח' או 'הוא יפתח'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יפעון הוא שילוב של שתי מילים עבריות: 'י' (קיצור של אלוהים) ו'פעון' (נגזר מ'פאה' שפירושו פתח). לפיכך, ניתן לפרש את השם יפעון כ'אלוהים יפתח' או 'הוא יפתח'. השם מופיע במקרא וקשור לאישיות מקראית.

in_greek.name: Ιαφθώ
in_greek.meaning: Ιαφθώ σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θα ανοίξει' ή 'ανοίγει'
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιαφθώ προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και συγκεκριμένα από τις λέξεις 'י' (σύντομο του Θεού) και 'פעון' (παράγωγο του 'פאה' που σημαίνει ανοίγω). Έτσι, το Ιαφθώ σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θα ανοίξει' ή 'ανοίγει'. Το όνομα αναφέρεται σε πρόσωπο της Παλαιάς Διαθήκης.

in_latin.name: Japheon
in_latin.meaning: Japheon means 'God will open' or 'He will open'
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Japheon is derived from Hebrew roots, combining 'y' (short for God) and 'pheon' (from 'pawah', meaning to open). Hence, Japheon can be interpreted as 'God will open' or 'He will open'. This name holds significance in biblical context.

in_english.name: Japheon
in_english.meaning: God will open or He will open
in_english.long_meaning: The name Japheon originates from Hebrew, combining 'y' (a shortened form of God) and 'pheon' (derived from 'pawah', meaning to open). Thus, Japheon signifies 'God will open' or 'He will open'. This name appears in biblical context, specifically in the book of Genesis, associated with Japheth, a son of Noah. The name symbolizes divine intervention and expansion. In Christian tradition, Japheon/Japheth represents a figure of faith and inheritance of divine blessings.

data.cultural_impact: Japheth carries a rich cultural significance as he is a prominent figure in the Judeo-Christian tradition. Japheth and his family are seen as the ancestors of many peoples around the world, including Europeans and Asians. This symbolic connection has been invoked throughout history to assert a common religious and cultural heritage, particularly in the context of the European discovery and colonization of other parts of the world. Further, many Christian names derived from Japheth evoke a sense of exploration, adventure, and foreignness, exemplified by the name "Japheon".
data.spiritual_significance: Japheth holds a significant spiritual meaning in the Judeo-Christian tradition as a symbol of God's expansive plan for humanity. The naming of Japheth as "God will add" highlights the idea of growth, expansion, and diversity in God's family. Furthermore, Japheth and his siblings Shem and Ham represent the unity and interconnectedness of all people in the eyes of God. On a personal level, the name Japheon can serve as a reminder of the vastness and complexity of God's plan and the importance of embracing the rich diversity of humanity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Japheth, in the Old Testament, is the third son of Noah and the progenitor of the Japhethites, or European peoples. His name means "God enlarges." This symbolizes the expansive nature of God's grace and love, extending beyond the boundaries of Noah's ark and reaching all nations.

biblical_reference.note: Japheth (the English form of Japheon) is mentioned as a son of Noah.

historical_references.reference: Genesis 5:32 - 'And Japheth lived after the death of Noah five hundred years; and thirty and five years after the flood.',
historical_references.context: Japheth is the third son of Noah and the oldest of his three sons who survived the flood. He is named after the Hebrew word for 'enlargement' or 'extension', and is believed to be the ancestor of many peoples, including the Greeks and Europeans.

historical_references.reference: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, Book 1, Chapter 6, Paragraph 2 - 'But the third son of Noah was Japheth, and he dwelt in the land of Greece, for which reason the Greeks are called by the surname of his name, as the Hellenes.'
historical_references.context: The Jewish historian Josephus writes that Japheth, the third son of Noah, is the ancestor of the Greeks. This reference demonstrates the influence of the biblical account on ancient Greek self-understanding.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Japheon continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Japheon from Dublin, Ireland embodies the meaning of Japheon - "God will add". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
